metadata.title: Privacy - HeapForge
metadata.description: A short overview of what operational logs and content request data HeapForge may handle.
metadata.ogDescription: A lightweight note on infrastructure logs, remote content requests, and supporting services.

privacy.title: What this project may keep track of
privacy.description: HeapForge runs as a technical archive without heavyweight personal data flows such as user accounts, payments, or comments. That said, the deployment stack and remote content infrastructure may still keep basic operational logs.

collection.title: Scope of collection
collection.body: The site does not currently store member accounts or profile data directly. However, the deployment platform, web server, and remote content API may retain operational details such as request time, request path, and response status.

usage.title: Why those logs exist
usage.body: Those signals are used for minimum operational needs such as incident tracing, performance checks, and remote content health verification. Even when search or discovery quality improves, system behavior is prioritized over personal identification.

vendors.title: Supporting services
vendors.body: Deployment infrastructure, image asset hosting, and remote content APIs may all participate in serving the docs experience. Retention windows and lower-level handling depend on the infrastructure operating each layer.

aside.title: Policy updates
aside.body: If the operating model changes, the changelog is updated first and this note is revised alongside it when needed.

metadata.title: Terms - HeapForge
metadata.description: Basic usage expectations for the HeapForge docs experience.

terms.title: The basic framing for using these docs
terms.description: HeapForge aims to be a long-lived technical archive, but every document is still bound to its moment, assumptions, and operating environment. These notes explain the baseline expectations around that reality.

reference.title: Reference-oriented content
reference.body: The material is written to support learning and real-world technical reference. Before applying any idea directly, it is still worth checking the latest official documentation and the exact environment you are working in.

availability.title: Things can change
availability.body: Project structure, content grouping, and remote content delivery rules may evolve over time. Some documents may still reflect older tradeoffs until they are refreshed, so freshness signals and the changelog should be read together.

links.title: External links and citations
links.body: Articles may include external references, tools, or service links. Their content and availability remain the responsibility of the external provider, and HeapForge does not guarantee them in real time.

aside.title: Related operating notes
aside.body: The contributor guide gives extra context on how content gets structured, validated, and promoted into the published docs flow.

metadata.title: Changelog - HeapForge
metadata.description: A short summary of recent updates across docs structure, search, and content operations.
metadata.ogDescription: Track the latest improvements around search contracts, remote validation, and contributor guidance.

changelog.title: Recent operating changes
changelog.description: This page groups the latest changes around discovery quality and editorial operations into a shorter reading surface. The detailed trail continues in worklogs and architecture notes.

search.title: Search ranking and preview alignment
search.body: Search ranking now treats title, summary, and in-body context more consistently, and the preview/highlight rules are shared between the `/docs?q=...` page and the `/api/search` response contract.

contracts.title: Remote content contract and observability
contracts.body: Remote payload schema validation has been tightened so upstream contract drift is easier to detect. Parse failures now leave clearer clues about which fields no longer match the expected document shape.

editorial.title: Contributor guide and published metadata checks
editorial.body: Published local documents now require explicit `status`, `updatedAt`, author metadata, read time, and topic label. A dedicated contributor guide also documents where to place files and what to verify before publishing.

aside.title: Follow the detailed history
aside.body: The GitHub repository and worklog documents continue the full trail behind these summaries.

hero.title: Architecting the Next Generation of Real-time Reactive Interfaces

body.intro: The transition from static data fetching to granular reactivity marks a deeper shift in how we design digital interaction. As low-latency products become more common, the infrastructure behind them needs to evolve beyond traditional state patterns.
body.streamParagraph: By leaning on stream-based state primitives, teams can reduce the cost of virtual DOM reconciliation in dense, high-frequency interfaces such as terminal views or financial dashboards.
body.mobileParagraph: The mobile experience comes with a different set of constraints. Precision here is not only visual; it becomes essential for maintaining clarity on smaller viewports.

paradox.title: The Reactivity Paradox
paradox.description: Modern web architecture often forces teams to fight their framework just to achieve the precision required by high-density interfaces. The challenge is reducing re-render scope while keeping the model declarative.
